what to know about heyclicky, privacy, and getting started.
what is heyclicky?
an ai buddy that lives on your mac. press the hotkey and it sees what you see, so you can ask it anything out loud and it’ll walk you through whatever you’re working on, or say “heyclicky agent” and it’ll go do the task for you.
is my data private?
yes. we only see your screen when you press the hotkey, and screenshots are never stored. we do keep basic text summaries so heyclicky has context. you can delete your account and all its data in settings.
is heyclicky watching my screen all the time?
no. we never look at your screen unless you press the hotkey.
what can heyclicky actually do?
it teaches you any tool, walks you through whatever you’re stuck on, draws right on your screen to point the way, and runs agents to do tasks for you.
what’s the difference between talk and agents?
talk is the conversation. ask anything, out loud, as much as you want. agents are heyclicky actually doing tasks for you, and those are counted per month on each plan.
which apps does it work with?
anything on your screen. if you can see it, heyclicky can see it. no plugins or integrations needed.
do i need a mac?
for now, yes. heyclicky is mac-only (sonoma 14.2 or higher). windows is coming, join the waitlist.
is it free?
you can start for free. when you’re ready for more, pro is $20/month and max is $100/month. cancel anytime.
what happens if i hit my agent limit?
talk keeps working, always. agent messages pause until your next cycle, or you can upgrade to max for 1,000 a month.
can i cancel anytime?
yes. everything is month-to-month, no lock-in. cancel in one click and keep access through the end of your cycle.

changelog
what's new
v
1.0.49
Sep 12, 2026
Introducing Clickys
Our biggest update yet. HeyClicky is 20 weeks old, and after 1.2 million messages we noticed we barely used agents ourselves. So we spent the last three weeks building a home for them that we'd actually want to open every day: a little team of Clickys, each with its own name, face, memory, and job. Tell them what's bugging you and they get to work ^-^
Watch the full video on YouTube.
getting started
A setup that gets to know you
:
Pick a character style, answer four quick questions about yourself and your work, and meet three Clickys made for you. The refreshed tour introduces them by name and shows you where to talk to them and find their suggestions.
Make a new Clicky through conversation
:
Tell HeyClicky what you'd like help with. It asks a few useful follow-ups, helps you think it through if you're unsure, and creates a Clicky with that job in mind. Your first time also includes a quick explanation of how Clickys work.
Setup doesn't spend your normal allowance
:
Onboarding and creating a Clicky have their own usage limits, so getting set up doesn't use your normal message, Clicky, or dictation allowance. Work you ask the Clicky to do afterward uses your plan as usual.
clickys & home
Clickys that stick around
:
Create a Clicky for whatever you're working on. Each has its own name, memory, conversation, and folder for its files. Come back tomorrow and pick up the same work without explaining everything again ^-^
A new home for your Clickys
:
We've updated the notch to make it the main home for your Clickys. Your Clickys, conversations, and files now live together in a full chat interface. Open it from the notch, the Dock, or Control + Command + A. Expand it into its own window when you want more room, then tuck it back into the notch. No model pickers, no settings maze. Just a chat and a hold-to-talk pill.
Make them yours
:
Choose from Dreamy Cloud and Puff Pals, then customize your Clicky's look. Their faces react as they listen, think, and talk, and doze off when you stop them (˘ω˘) The same face and color follow the Clicky into the notch and the card at the top right while it works.
Keep your people close
:
Pin your go-to Clickys, search your conversations, and archive chats you're done with. Status indicators show who's working, who needs you, and which results you haven't read yet.
Your earlier work is still here
:
Everything you ran in older versions is still here. Flip the legacy toggle in Settings and it shows up in your Clickys list. Open one to continue the work, or move it into a new or existing Clicky. HeyClicky asks before moving it and carries the earlier work along.
voice & conversations
Just talk to your Clicky
:
Hold your voice shortcut in a Clicky's chat to give it a task or follow up directly. Your words land in that conversation. Type whenever you prefer, and send changes while it works without losing your original request.
Ask from anywhere
:
You don't have to open Home to work with them. From any app, ask 'what's running right now?', 'tell Launch Scout I like this shirt too', or 'make me a Clicky that cleans my desktop every morning', and HeyClicky routes it to the right one or founds a new one.
Follow-ups know who you mean
:
Ask "how's it going?", "what did it find?", or "retry it" and HeyClicky uses the Clicky's progress, recent results, and the chat you were just viewing. Spoken updates name the Clicky, so "yeah, do that" can go back to the right one.
See the work as it happens
:
Live progress appears in the conversation, with the work steps tucked away once a task finishes. Stop a task, retry a failed one, or let different Clickys work on separate jobs. Approved suggestions waiting on a busy Clicky stay in that Clicky's queue.
Easier to read long chats
:
Older messages load as you scroll up, new replies leave you where you're reading, and a jump-to-latest button gets you back. Conversations and their scroll positions are remembered when you switch away and return.
HeyClicky remembers more of your recent conversations (40 messages, up from 20), plus everything you said in the onboarding interview.
files, apps & settings
Bring files into the conversation
:
Drag files into a Clicky's chat, attach them, or paste files and images with Command + V. You can send an attachment on its own, and previews make it easier to see what you're sharing.
Open the result right beside the chat
:
Preview documents, PDFs, and images inside Home, expand them for a closer look, or open them in their app or Finder. Each chat remembers its own open document, and Markdown previews update as the file changes. Animated images play in documents too.
Connect your own tools
:
Add custom MCP connections alongside the built-in app catalog, using a server URL or a local command. Supported connections can sign in through your browser or use an API key. HeyClicky reads what the connector can do so your Clickys know when to use it.
Clearer connection status
:
Apps show when they're connecting, ready, or need you to sign in again. Connecting or changing a tool updates what the voice assistant knows about it, without waiting for a fresh conversation.
Settings, at home
:
Manage apps, account settings, voices, and shortcuts inside Home. Voice previews and shortcut recording are easier to reach, and the update control tells you whether to download an update or install and relaunch.
Skills are on pause
:
We've removed Skills for now. We're still figuring out the right way to make them useful, and we plan to bring them back in a new form. If you miss them, please let us know on WhatsApp or at hi@heyclicky.com. Tell us what you used them for <3
suggestions
Suggestions made for you
:
Clickys dig into recent work in your connected apps and relevant web research to suggest concrete things they can help with. Suggestions have their own place in the sidebar, with one idea at a time. Research uses read-only access to supported connected apps; the proposed task waits for your go-ahead.
Say yes, skip, or adjust it
:
Say "do it" to start the suggestion you're looking at, or "show me the next one" to skip. Want something a little different? Hit Adjust and talk through the change. You can cancel and come back to the same proposal.
A little morning hello
:
When morning ideas are ready, your Clickys can pop out of the notch with a short greeting and a Show me button. The invitation waits when HeyClicky detects a call, screen sharing, or Focus mode, and stops reminding you once you've opened Suggestions or dismissed it.
Deeper research behind them
:
We rebuilt the whole pipeline: one researcher per connected app plus the public web, reading full documents from the last 72 hours, then an editor picks the ideas worth your time. Say no to one and tell it why, and tomorrow's batch takes that into account.
routines
Put repeat tasks on a routine
:
Ask a Clicky to repeat a task, like "give me a daily briefing" or "check this every few hours". Routines run on this Mac while HeyClicky is open. Open the Clicky's profile to pause, resume, run now, or delete one.
Results without the interruption
:
Routine results arrive in the same chat with an unread indicator, without a spoken announcement or completion chime. If your Mac was asleep, a missed routine catches up once after waking instead of piling up every missed run.
Recovery built in
:
Routines wait while you're offline or their Clicky is busy, and retry failed work after a short delay. Paused routines stay paused, and archiving a Clicky pauses its routines too.
computer use
You decide when a Clicky can control your Mac
:
Before it clicks or types, a Clicky asks for permission in its chat and the floating panel at the top right. Choose "Allow once", "Always allow", or "Not now", or answer by voice. Extra-usage approval requests can be answered by voice too.
A separate browser window
:
Browser tasks can use their own window in Chrome and other Chromium browsers, using your signed-in profile. For work on the page you're already viewing, HeyClicky asks whether to use that tab or a separate window. Non-Chromium browsers may fall back to opening a tab.
improved & fixed
Permission setup is less fussy
:
Fixed duplicate permission prompts and stuck setup transitions. The Screen Recording guide points to the screen-and-audio list when it can identify it, permission retries stay available, and skipping the tour clears its drawings and speech.
Clearer sounds and replies
:
Refreshed the sounds for task starts, finishes, and requests for help. Completion announcements are less likely to go missing or get clipped at the start, and cancelling a suggestion adjustment stops its pending speech too.
Team checkout accepts promo codes
:
Team admins can now enter a promotion code directly at checkout.
Lighter on your Mac
:
Home idles at 3 to 5% CPU and switching between Clickys stays under 5%. Our first build sat at 36 to 43% doing nothing and pegged a whole core while a Clicky worked, so we fixed that before shipping.
Bluetooth headphones
:
Finish cues pre-roll so a cold connection can't swallow them, and the squeak at the start of the first spoken reply is gone.
Dictation works with Home open, and only lands in Home's composer when Home actually has focus. A background window never steals words meant for another app.
On a Studio Display or other external monitor, the menu bar read as a permanently open menu, so voice holds fell back to the spoken router and Escape got swallowed. Fixed.
The screen permission card could stay stuck on 'Pick a display' after you'd already granted access.
Buttons on the top-right card could miss their targets, and the Clicky list reordered itself while Clickys worked.
Clicky chats stalling on launch with a long history, live work lost across a relaunch, and morning suggestions silently never showing up after a relaunch.

title: trust & privacy · heyclicky
text:
the fine print
what happens to your data
screen
we only see your screen when you press the hotkey, heyclicky doesn't continuously look at your screen.
storage
we never store your raw screenshots. they're gone after they're processed. we do keep the ai generated screenshot analysis and your prompt.
processing
nothing is done locally. everything is processed in the cloud where we forward the request to either anthropic or openai.
deletion
want your data gone? just ask. we'll permanently delete it, any time.
training
we never train on your data. neither do our providers (anthropic, openai). their terms don't allow it.
background
in the background, clicky collects nothing. no keystrokes, no clipboard, no files, no screen. when you hit the hotkey, it just notes your open apps and the domain of your current tab.
quitting
close the app and it's closed. no background services, no telemetry, nothing keeps running.
analytics
the only third parties we share with are posthog, for product analytics, and sentry, for crash reports. they never see your screenshots or screen.
certifications
no soc 2 or iso 27001 yet.

what is heyclicky?
an ai buddy that lives on your mac. press the hotkey and it sees what you see, so you can ask it anything out loud and it’ll walk you through whatever you’re working on, or say “heyclicky agent” and it’ll go do the task for you.
is my data private?
yes. we only see your screen when you press the hotkey, and screenshots are never stored. we do keep basic text summaries so heyclicky has context. you can delete your account and all its data in settings.
is heyclicky watching my screen all the time?
no. we never look at your screen unless you press the hotkey.
what can heyclicky actually do?
it teaches you any tool, walks you through whatever you’re stuck on, draws right on your screen to point the way, and runs agents to do tasks for you.
what’s the difference between talk and agents?
talk is the conversation. ask anything, out loud, as much as you want. agents are heyclicky actually doing tasks for you, and those are counted per month on each plan.
which apps does it work with?
anything on your screen. if you can see it, heyclicky can see it. no plugins or integrations needed.
do i need a mac?
for now, yes. heyclicky is mac-only (sonoma 14.2 or higher). windows is coming, join the waitlist.
is it free?
you can start for free. when you’re ready for more, pro is $20/month and max is $100/month. cancel anytime.
what happens if i hit my agent limit?
talk keeps working, always. agent messages pause until your next cycle, or you can upgrade to max for 1,000 a month.
can i cancel anytime?
yes. everything is month-to-month, no lock-in. cancel in one click and keep access through the end of your cycle.

This privacy policy applies to the heyclicky website and macOS application and governs the use of services provided by heyclicky to its users.
1. Notice

3.2 Third party AI providers

3.3 Data storage and security
Your data is stored securely on our servers and is protected using industry-standard encryption and security practices. We retain your data for the period necessary to fulfill the purposes outlined in this Privacy Policy unless a longer retention period is required or permitted by law.
3.4 Sharing of user data

When third parties are employed to process user data on our behalf, they do so under confidentiality agreements and are obligated to comply with our privacy policy and data protection laws.

Outside these specified categories, no external party will have access to your personal information, unless you explicitly give us permission. Should we wish to share your information with an external party outside of these categories, we will always seek your explicit consent first.
4. Retention of information
We retain your information for as long as necessary to provide you with heyclicky's services. All personally identifiable information will be deleted upon your request to cease using our services, such as when you delete your account or when you explicitly request its deletion. 5. Your rights
As the owner of your information and in accordance with the GDPR, you are entitled to several rights regarding the handling of your data by heyclicky:

6. Opting out

You have the option to opt out of these services at any time. To unsubscribe from our email communications, simply click the unsubscribe link located at the bottom of any of our emails.
7. Security of your information
At heyclicky, we employ multiple measures to protect your data to the fullest extent possible. These measures include:
Using security software, such as virus scanners.
Implementing TLS (Transport Layer Security) to ensure secure connections between our servers and your device.
Adhering to internet standards like DKIM, SPF, and DMARC for the protection of our email traffic.
8. Changes to this policy

If you do not agree with the modifications to the policy, you have the opportunity to withdraw your consent during this notification period.

frequently asked questions

what is heyclicky?
an ai buddy that lives on your mac. press the hotkey and it sees what you see, so you can ask it anything out loud and it’ll walk you through whatever you’re working on, or say “heyclicky agent” and it’ll go do the task for you.
is my data private?
yes. we only see your screen when you press the hotkey, and screenshots are never stored. we do keep basic text summaries so heyclicky has context. you can delete your account and all its data in settings.
is heyclicky watching my screen all the time?
no. we never look at your screen unless you press the hotkey.
what can heyclicky actually do?
it teaches you any tool, walks you through whatever you’re stuck on, draws right on your screen to point the way, and runs agents to do tasks for you.
what’s the difference between talk and agents?
talk is the conversation. ask anything, out loud, as much as you want. agents are heyclicky actually doing tasks for you, and those are counted per month on each plan.
which apps does it work with?
anything on your screen. if you can see it, heyclicky can see it. no plugins or integrations needed.
do i need a mac?
for now, yes. heyclicky is mac-only (sonoma 14.2 or higher). windows is coming, join the waitlist.
is it free?
you can start for free. when you’re ready for more, pro is $20/month and max is $100/month. cancel anytime.
what happens if i hit my agent limit?
talk keeps working, always. agent messages pause until your next cycle, or you can upgrade to max for 1,000 a month.
can i cancel anytime?
yes. everything is month-to-month, no lock-in. cancel in one click and keep access through the end of your cycle.

1.0.49
Sep 12, 2026
Introducing Clickys
Our biggest update yet. HeyClicky is 20 weeks old, and after 1.2 million messages we noticed we barely used agents ourselves. So we spent the last three weeks building a home for them that we'd actually want to open every day: a little team of Clickys, each with its own name, face, memory, and job. Tell them what's bugging you and they get to work ^-^
Watch the full video on YouTube.
getting started
A setup that gets to know you
:
Pick a character style, answer four quick questions about yourself and your work, and meet three Clickys made for you. The refreshed tour introduces them by name and shows you where to talk to them and find their suggestions.
Make a new Clicky through conversation
:
Tell HeyClicky what you'd like help with. It asks a few useful follow-ups, helps you think it through if you're unsure, and creates a Clicky with that job in mind. Your first time also includes a quick explanation of how Clickys work.
Setup doesn't spend your normal allowance
:
Onboarding and creating a Clicky have their own usage limits, so getting set up doesn't use your normal message, Clicky, or dictation allowance. Work you ask the Clicky to do afterward uses your plan as usual.
clickys & home
Clickys that stick around
:
Create a Clicky for whatever you're working on. Each has its own name, memory, conversation, and folder for its files. Come back tomorrow and pick up the same work without explaining everything again ^-^
A new home for your Clickys
:
We've updated the notch to make it the main home for your Clickys. Your Clickys, conversations, and files now live together in a full chat interface. Open it from the notch, the Dock, or Control + Command + A. Expand it into its own window when you want more room, then tuck it back into the notch. No model pickers, no settings maze. Just a chat and a hold-to-talk pill.
Make them yours
:
Choose from Dreamy Cloud and Puff Pals, then customize your Clicky's look. Their faces react as they listen, think, and talk, and doze off when you stop them (˘ω˘) The same face and color follow the Clicky into the notch and the card at the top right while it works.
Keep your people close
:
Pin your go-to Clickys, search your conversations, and archive chats you're done with. Status indicators show who's working, who needs you, and which results you haven't read yet.
Your earlier work is still here
:
Everything you ran in older versions is still here. Flip the legacy toggle in Settings and it shows up in your Clickys list. Open one to continue the work, or move it into a new or existing Clicky. HeyClicky asks before moving it and carries the earlier work along.
voice & conversations
Just talk to your Clicky
:
Hold your voice shortcut in a Clicky's chat to give it a task or follow up directly. Your words land in that conversation. Type whenever you prefer, and send changes while it works without losing your original request.
Ask from anywhere
:
You don't have to open Home to work with them. From any app, ask 'what's running right now?', 'tell Launch Scout I like this shirt too', or 'make me a Clicky that cleans my desktop every morning', and HeyClicky routes it to the right one or founds a new one.
Follow-ups know who you mean
:
Ask "how's it going?", "what did it find?", or "retry it" and HeyClicky uses the Clicky's progress, recent results, and the chat you were just viewing. Spoken updates name the Clicky, so "yeah, do that" can go back to the right one.
See the work as it happens
:
Live progress appears in the conversation, with the work steps tucked away once a task finishes. Stop a task, retry a failed one, or let different Clickys work on separate jobs. Approved suggestions waiting on a busy Clicky stay in that Clicky's queue.
Easier to read long chats
:
Older messages load as you scroll up, new replies leave you where you're reading, and a jump-to-latest button gets you back. Conversations and their scroll positions are remembered when you switch away and return.
HeyClicky remembers more of your recent conversations (40 messages, up from 20), plus everything you said in the onboarding interview.
files, apps & settings
Bring files into the conversation
:
Drag files into a Clicky's chat, attach them, or paste files and images with Command + V. You can send an attachment on its own, and previews make it easier to see what you're sharing.
Open the result right beside the chat
:
Preview documents, PDFs, and images inside Home, expand them for a closer look, or open them in their app or Finder. Each chat remembers its own open document, and Markdown previews update as the file changes. Animated images play in documents too.
Connect your own tools
:
Add custom MCP connections alongside the built-in app catalog, using a server URL or a local command. Supported connections can sign in through your browser or use an API key. HeyClicky reads what the connector can do so your Clickys know when to use it.
Clearer connection status
:
Apps show when they're connecting, ready, or need you to sign in again. Connecting or changing a tool updates what the voice assistant knows about it, without waiting for a fresh conversation.
Settings, at home
:
Manage apps, account settings, voices, and shortcuts inside Home. Voice previews and shortcut recording are easier to reach, and the update control tells you whether to download an update or install and relaunch.
Skills are on pause
:
We've removed Skills for now. We're still figuring out the right way to make them useful, and we plan to bring them back in a new form. If you miss them, please let us know on WhatsApp or at hi@heyclicky.com. Tell us what you used them for <3
suggestions
Suggestions made for you
:
Clickys dig into recent work in your connected apps and relevant web research to suggest concrete things they can help with. Suggestions have their own place in the sidebar, with one idea at a time. Research uses read-only access to supported connected apps; the proposed task waits for your go-ahead.
Say yes, skip, or adjust it
:
Say "do it" to start the suggestion you're looking at, or "show me the next one" to skip. Want something a little different? Hit Adjust and talk through the change. You can cancel and come back to the same proposal.
A little morning hello
:
When morning ideas are ready, your Clickys can pop out of the notch with a short greeting and a Show me button. The invitation waits when HeyClicky detects a call, screen sharing, or Focus mode, and stops reminding you once you've opened Suggestions or dismissed it.
Deeper research behind them
:
We rebuilt the whole pipeline: one researcher per connected app plus the public web, reading full documents from the last 72 hours, then an editor picks the ideas worth your time. Say no to one and tell it why, and tomorrow's batch takes that into account.
routines
Put repeat tasks on a routine
:
Ask a Clicky to repeat a task, like "give me a daily briefing" or "check this every few hours". Routines run on this Mac while HeyClicky is open. Open the Clicky's profile to pause, resume, run now, or delete one.
Results without the interruption
:
Routine results arrive in the same chat with an unread indicator, without a spoken announcement or completion chime. If your Mac was asleep, a missed routine catches up once after waking instead of piling up every missed run.
Recovery built in
:
Routines wait while you're offline or their Clicky is busy, and retry failed work after a short delay. Paused routines stay paused, and archiving a Clicky pauses its routines too.
computer use
You decide when a Clicky can control your Mac
:
Before it clicks or types, a Clicky asks for permission in its chat and the floating panel at the top right. Choose "Allow once", "Always allow", or "Not now", or answer by voice. Extra-usage approval requests can be answered by voice too.
A separate browser window
:
Browser tasks can use their own window in Chrome and other Chromium browsers, using your signed-in profile. For work on the page you're already viewing, HeyClicky asks whether to use that tab or a separate window. Non-Chromium browsers may fall back to opening a tab.
improved & fixed
Permission setup is less fussy
:
Fixed duplicate permission prompts and stuck setup transitions. The Screen Recording guide points to the screen-and-audio list when it can identify it, permission retries stay available, and skipping the tour clears its drawings and speech.
Clearer sounds and replies
:
Refreshed the sounds for task starts, finishes, and requests for help. Completion announcements are less likely to go missing or get clipped at the start, and cancelling a suggestion adjustment stops its pending speech too.
Team checkout accepts promo codes
:
Team admins can now enter a promotion code directly at checkout.
Lighter on your Mac
:
Home idles at 3 to 5% CPU and switching between Clickys stays under 5%. Our first build sat at 36 to 43% doing nothing and pegged a whole core while a Clicky worked, so we fixed that before shipping.
Bluetooth headphones
:
Finish cues pre-roll so a cold connection can't swallow them, and the squeak at the start of the first spoken reply is gone.
Dictation works with Home open, and only lands in Home's composer when Home actually has focus. A background window never steals words meant for another app.
On a Studio Display or other external monitor, the menu bar read as a permanently open menu, so voice holds fell back to the spoken router and Escape got swallowed. Fixed.
The screen permission card could stay stuck on 'Pick a display' after you'd already granted access.
Buttons on the top-right card could miss their targets, and the Clicky list reordered itself while Clickys worked.

Spatial context, skills, proactive agents, memory
Four launches in one go, all in production now. If you have any questions on how this stuff works, just ask!
spatial context
Point, circle, scribble
:
When you talk to HeyClicky, you'll notice a little trail of paint it leaves behind. Draw on your screen to point at or circle the specific thing you want the AI to focus on. Especially useful when you have a lot going on, like complex editing software or a complicated diagram. It's very intuitive, try it out!
Spatial context in action. Click to watch the full video.
skills
A skills library
:
Skills literally give AI superpowers, but installing them from random GitHub links is annoying. So we built a library: hover your notch, click add skill, and activate any of about 100 community-built skills in one click. When you talk to HeyClicky or run an agent, the skill is active. Want your own? Hit "Create a skill" and type what it should do.
The community skills library, one click to activate.
proactive agents
Agents that suggest themselves
:
99% of people don't even know the extent of an agent's power, so how would you know what to ask for? Every morning and afternoon, HeyClicky recommends two personalized agents at the top right of your screen. All you gotta do is click approve. We found ourselves getting magical recommendations for agents we had no idea we even needed.
(A note from the future: we later turned proactive agents off over privacy unease. See v1.0.46 above.)
Suggested agents, one click to approve.
memory
It remembers
:
The more you use HeyClicky, the more it remembers. Your name, your language, how you like your CSVs named, everything. Under the hood it maintains two files: PROFILE.md for your habits and general preferences, and VOLATILE.md for the project you're working on right now. Both get injected into the voice model and the agent.
